title: InfraOps Support Engineer, Operations Management Center (OMC)
descriptionHtml:
The InfraOps Support Engineer is a Tier 1 support engineer in Amazon's Operations Management Center (OMC) - a 24/7/365 team that keeps the technology inside Amazon's 400+ corporate office buildings running across Networking, Audio-Visual (AV), and Print services. This engineer is the first line of response for office-infrastructure incidents.

Operating within the Amazon Support Engineer (SupEng) job family, the engineer provides high-quality support across all three service areas while beginning to develop deep subject-matter expertise in one or more focus areas, for which they become the technical point of contact on their team. They respond, triage and resolve incidents within target times using established procedures, detect trends before they become problems, contribute to and refine the team's operating procedures, and mentor more junior engineers. Success requires the ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative, shift-based environment.

Key job responsibilities
On a typical shift, an InfraOps Support Engineer will:

1. Monitor, Detect & Triage

Be the first line of response and keep ahead of problems.

Triage incoming incidents (tickets) within defined target response times, using judgment to resolve in place or route to the responsible team.

Use dashboards, alarms, and other tools for Networking, AV, and Print services across the global building fleet, interpreting what those signals indicate to solve incidents.

Detect ongoing trends or emerging problems before they occur and define proactive actions to prevent customer impact.

Assess incident scope and severity, correlate related incidents into a single parent incident, and prioritise work against SLAs.

2. Troubleshoot & Support

Resolve issues and support the team's products and systems.

Provide high-quality Tier 1 support for the products and systems in the team's scope, resolving straightforward problems with limited documentation and minimal escalation.

Support critical issues using existing runbooks; maintain composure through difficult interactions until the issue is resolved.

Perform on-call duties on a rotating schedule and respond to emergent events.

Escalate appropriately when resolution requires significant deviation from procedure or when an issue becomes a risk.

3. Subject-Matter Expertise & Technical Leadership

Grow into the go-to person for a focus area.

Develop and apply expertise in one or more focus areas (e.g., Networking, AV, or Print), acting as the technical point of contact for that area within the team.

Give technical direction to others and impart knowledge to users, customers, and teammates.

Lead internal team projects and deliver on defined goals and timelines.

4. Documentation & Operational Improvement

Improve how the team operates.

Identify areas to improve support documentation and processes, and author new runbooks/SOPs and knowledge-base articles where gaps exist.

Identify improvements to existing and new support tools that increase operational efficiency, and help drive their implementation.

Help develop and refine the operational policies and procedures used by the team.

5. Mentoring & Collaboration

Raise the bar for the team.

Serve as a mentor to junior engineers and act as a training buddy for new hires; may assist in hiring activities.

Maintain good working relationships across Amazon and work cross-functionally with partner teams to solve problems and improve processes.

Communicate infrastructure health and trends clearly, both in real time and as inputs to weekly/monthly business reviews.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working with Windows server technologies: AD, DFS, Print Services, SCCM
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
- Experience in IT client, server, and network service delivery
- Experience with networking technology (TCP/IP, subnetting, DNS and DHCP)
- Experience supporting Windows, Mac and/or Linux operating systems in a corporate setting
- Experience working in large-scale networking environments
- High school diploma, or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in computer networking
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in Network protocols like DNS/DHCP/TCP
- Experience supporting video-conference and teleconference equipment.

title: Sr. Inventory and Asset Manager, Inventory and Asset Management
descriptionHtml:
Sr. Inventory and Asset Management role is responsible for leading the development, implementation, and sustainability of an innovative and scalable AR-wide inventory management framework. This role involves collaborating closely with internal supply chain teams, external partner teams (Deployment, Field IT, RME, and Shared Services), and SC supported customer business units (AMZL, ATS, GCF, and GSF) to ensure alignment and successful execution across all stakeholders. They lead the strategic development and deployment of a system-driven inventory audit and cycle count process across a network of over 5,000 sites. A key component of this framework is the implementation and maintenance of data-driven inventory thresholds for more than 12,000 distinct IT products, managing $950MM inventory across 5000+ sites and approximately $600 MM inventory across 13 Rapid Asset Deployment (RAD) centers. Leveraging their analytical expertise, they integrate diverse, multifaceted data sources such as item-specific site-type Bill of Materials (BOM), operational criticality, cost, lead time, and historical demand patterns (including ad-hoc, peak/prime, and ARMA) to drive the dynamic ABC classification across IT product catalogue and define their optimal threshold levels across IT hubs and RAD centers. The role also leads the strategic management of inventory levels for Amazon-owned inventory stored at RADs, VARs, and 3PLs along-side the Field IT Hubs. It involves establishing and executing a standardized process to systematically reduce excess and obsolete (E&O) inventory, valued at over $50+ MM across the Field IT Hubs along-with the implementation of robust controls to ensure the available inventory across the network is effectively leveraged and consumed in accordance with the established policies. In pursuit of cost optimization for Amazon, the role entails the critical task of repurposing, returning, or reselling inventory, guided by stringent eligibility criteria established within the inventory management framework and in alignment with contractual obligations delineated in VAR/OEM agreements. They build and define the business-essential tier-1 and tier-2 inventory and asset metrics which include Optimal Inventory Thresholds (inventory health), Inventory Accuracy Percentage, Asset Shrinkage Percentage, Inventory Availability (Days of Cover), Aged Inventory (slow-moving), Net Book Value reporting, and Excess/Obsolete Inventory as a percentage of total inventory. These metrics determine and advise SC partners and customers on optimal ordering timing for 2.9MM infrastructure and 14.9MM end-user equipment, ensuring orders are placed under lead times, create funding predictions, inventory requirements/rebalancing in the network to support 30+ demand streams encompassing 350+ new site launches, 18+ customer programs, and 27+ lifecycle initiatives, enabling SC to provide an insight-based & data-driven service to customers to operate their business

title: Senior Construction Manager, Quick Commerce
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Quick Commerce team is revolutionizing the customer experience through sub-30-minute delivery by rapidly scaling a first-of-its-kind micro-fulfillment network across North America. We are seeking an experienced Senior Construction Manager to serve as a individual contributor responsible for the construction execution and delivery of a portfolio of complex projects.

This role is ideal for an experienced builder who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and can independently drive projects through accelerated schedules, evolving requirements, and complex field conditions. The Senior Construction Manager will own construction execution from contractor procurement and mobilization through substantial completion, Certificate of Occupancy, turnover, and launch readiness.

The Senior Construction Manager will partner closely with Pre-Construction, Real Estate, Design, Launch, Operations, Procurement, Legal, and external consultants while directly managing General Contractors and vendors across multiple concurrent projects. This individual will be accountable for delivering projects safely, on schedule, within approved budgets, and to Amazon’s quality and operational standards.

Successful candidates bring deep experience in construction management, development, general contracting, architecture, engineering, or owner-side project delivery. The ideal candidate combines strong technical and field expertise with operational rigor, sound judgment, executive communication skills, and the ability to independently resolve complex construction challenges.

Key job responsibilities
- Own construction execution across a portfolio of Quick Commerce tenant improvement and conversion projects from contractor award through substantial completion, Certificate of Occupancy, turnover, and launch.
- Manage General Contractors, vendors, and consultants, ensuring performance against scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety expectations.
- Lead construction RFPs, bid leveling, contractor selection, and GMP development; present budgets, risks, and recommendations to leadership.
- Establish and manage project budgets, schedules, scopes, and critical milestones in partnership with internal and external stakeholders.
- Serve as Amazon’s primary point of contact during construction, driving alignment across contractors, Design, Pre-Construction, Operations, Launch, landlords, and consultants.
- Monitor progress through site visits, OAC meetings, schedule reviews, and milestone tracking; proactively identify risks and drive mitigation and recovery plans.
- Manage RFIs, submittals, change orders, unforeseen conditions, and schedule impacts while maintaining appropriate cost and schedule controls.
- Coordinate resolution of MEP, life safety, utility, permitting, inspection, and jurisdictional issues impacting project delivery.
- Lead project closeout, commissioning, punch list completion, documentation, and operational turnover.
- Drive continuous improvement and lessons learned to reduce costs, shorten timelines, improve quality, and standardize construction execution across the portfolio.

Travel up to 60%.

A day in the life
A typical day may start with reviewing construction schedules, budgets, and critical risks across several active projects, followed by OAC meetings with General Contractors, designers, and consultants. You’ll partner throughout the day with Pre-Construction, Design, Real Estate, Procurement, Launch, and Operations teams to resolve field conditions, RFIs, change orders, permitting challenges, and upcoming milestones. Site visits provide opportunities to validate progress, quality, safety, and operational readiness firsthand. You’ll work directly with contractors to remove roadblocks and develop recovery plans when needed, ensuring projects remain on track for turnover and launch for our Operations customers.

About the team
Amazon’s Quick Commerce Construction team is building the infrastructure behind a new way for customers to receive everyday essentials faster. Our mission is to deliver safe, high-quality spaces at speed while balancing cost, quality, and operational needs. We operate with a builder mentality: challenging traditional construction timelines, simplifying where possible, and developing solutions that can scale. Our culture values ownership, curiosity, collaboration, and practical problem-solving. We work across disciplines to test new approaches, learn quickly, and continuously improve how we build. Ultimately, we are turning ambitious delivery concepts into physical spaces enabling a faster, more convenient customer experience.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years of relevant discipline work, or 5+ years of construction or project management experience
- 5+ years of experience negotiating construction, procurement and labor contracts
- 5+ years of project management, real estate development, architecture/design experience

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Structural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
- 10+ years of construction or project management, or 10+ years of relevant discipline work experience

title: IT Support Engineer, Ring IT
descriptionHtml:
Ring IT is hiring an IT Support Engineer II for our Hawthorne, CA headquarters (LAX32). You'll be one of two on-site technical leads for an office of about 440 employees, and this is a fully on-site role.

You'll own the day-to-day technology experience for everyone at the site, from senior executives and their assistants to new hires on their first morning. That covers:

Mac and Windows hardware, imaging and asset management
Identity and access, including onboarding and offboarding
Conference room and event AV
The collaboration tools Ring's engineers, designers and business teams use every day: Slack, Jira, Confluence, TestRail and Figma
You'll also support remote employees, shipping configured equipment and resolving issues over chat and video.

At this level, you're expected to work through difficult and ambiguous problems to root cause without a playbook. You'll spot patterns across tickets, coordinate fixes with partner teams, and keep customers informed until the issue is closed. Partner teams include Amazon corporate IT, Security and Facilities. You'll lead site projects, such as lab network extensions, office changes and executive events.

Ring IT is moving toward self-service and AI-enabled support. We want someone who writes scripts and uses AI tools to remove repetitive work rather than repeat it. You'll mentor peers and serve as an escalation point for the broader support team.

Key job responsibilities
Site support and customer experience
Provide high-touch, discreet support to senior leaders (VP and above) and their executive assistants
Handle walk-up, ticket and Slack support across hardware, software, network and access issues, and find the root cause of difficult problems
Set up and troubleshoot conference rooms and meeting AV, and support executive events, demos and all-hands meetings
Share site coverage with your peer engineer to keep the office staffed throughout business hours, with occasional after-hours support

Identity, access and lifecycle
Run employee onboarding, offboarding and internal transfers, including timely access removal and asset recovery
Provision access and administer Slack, Jira/Confluence (projects and spaces), TestRail and Figma

Hardware and assets
Image, deploy, ship and track laptops, loaners, mobile test devices, peripherals and security keys
Manage equipment returns and e-waste, keeping asset records accurate

Escalation and improvement
Detect issues affecting many users, document the pattern, and escalate to partner teams until resolved
Automate repeatable work with scripts and AI tools, and write and maintain runbooks and knowledge-base articles
Lead site projects such as lab network extensions and office changes
Mentor peers and serve as an escalation point for the support team

A day in the life
Your morning starts in the LAX32 IT room with walk-ups: a new hire's Mac that won't enroll, a lost security key. An executive assistant pings you: their VP's all-hands starts in an hour and the room display won't connect. Back at your desk, you work the queue: a batch of application access requests, a new Jira project. When a dozen users hit the same compliance error, you write up the pattern and escalate it. You check in with your site partner to plan tomorrow's coverage, then script away a repetitive task before heading out.

About the team
Ring IT supports Ring employees across US and international offices. Our work spans four pillars: IT Support, IT Security, Builder Collaboration and AI Enablement. At LAX32, you and one other site engineer share responsibility for covering the office throughout business hours. You'll plan your schedules together and step in for each other during time off and appointments. Occasional after-hours work is required for events and urgent issues. You'll work with systems and development engineers who build our automation. We value ownership, curiosity, and builders who would rather automate a problem than solve it twice.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of technical support experience
- 4+ years of corporate setting Windows, Mac or Linux Operating systems support experience
- 4+ years of PC repair, troubleshooting, deployment and liquidation experience
- Bachelor's degree in IT, computer science or equivalent
- Experience in direct customer engagement, with a focus on support to senior executives (Vice President and C-level)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience supporting video conference and teleconference equipment
- Experience with networking technology (TCP/IP, subnetting, DNS and DHCP)
- Experience in technical support, or experience scripting in one or more language (e.g. Bash, Python, Perl, Ruby)
- Experience using AI-assisted development tools in academic or professional settings

title: Senior Site EHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we prioritize health, safety, and well-being above all else. There is nothing more important. To support this priority, Amazon is seeking an experienced and innovative Senior Site Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Manager to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for partnering with the site level operations team for your designated site in order to execute company WHS policies and ensure compliance to all applicable local and regional regulations. By leveraging lean principles and Kaizen events, you will lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce conditional and ergonomic risk in Amazon’s processes to ensure a safe and healthful working environment for our associates.

In this role, you must demonstrate the ability to build trust and confidence with the cross functional operations teams, and influence change through providing comprehensive risk assessments and safety data analysis. To do so, you must be an effective communicator and send clear, concise and consistent messages, both verbally and in writing. You will also be required to instruct and train operations leadership and site WHS professionals in company EHS policies while assisting the regional teams in incorporating our safety standards at their sites. Your experience working in safety programs and your relevant safety, environmental and ergonomic knowledge in an operations environment will be crucial. You will be responsible for developing a team of safety managers and safety professionals at your designated site. Your teams’ success will depend on your ability to create and execute leadership development plans for your larger team. You must demonstrate your ability to clearly communicate organizational direction through your team. As a senior leader in the WHS organization, you will also be responsible for judging and assessing safety talent to select appropriate bench strength for current and future business needs.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Act as SME of local/regional regulations and company WHS policy.
- Provide guidance and oversight to ensure compliance to all applicable Amazon Safety Policies.
- Measure site performance against published requirements in safety policies. For all deficiencies, identify a plan for the site to implement and fix all identified deficiencies.
- Ensure safety record keeping and data integrity and provides Operations with accurate reporting and metrics to support business safety initiatives.

- Audit the workplace organization and Associate behaviors to ensure that training, auditing and scoring methods are accurate and consistent.
- Manage and mentor the Safety Managers and Safety Associates in your assigned site.
- Engage the Injury Prevention Specialists (IPS) and Site Leadership to drive long-term strategic actions to achieve incident reduction.
- Perform targeted Kaizen events in partnership with the Operations teams based on the risks identified in each task (force, repetition, and awkward postures).
- Ensure site leadership and associates are trained and knowledgeable of their responsibilities under each policy.
- Audit the quality, delivery (including qualifications of the trainer), and effectiveness of all required safety training.
- Review for effectiveness the deployed safety tools and revise to ensure continual improvement.
- Partner with corporate and other regional field safety personnel to leverage global safety and environmental best practices into NA network standards.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

title: Software Development Engineer II, AWS DynamoDB
descriptionHtml:
Amazon DynamoDB powers many of the world's fastest-growing businesses, including Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin. It also powers enterprises such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One. Within Amazon, it runs high-traffic properties including Alexa, Amazon.com, and every Amazon fulfillment center. DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world. We believe it is always Day 1, and we keep improving the service and adding new capabilities.

DynamoDB customers count on consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, high availability, and durable data. Testing is how DynamoDB keeps those promises with every change it ships. The Test Infrastructure team builds test frameworks that every DynamoDB engineer uses to validate features, run integration and performance tests, and qualify releases. When test infrastructure is fast and reliable, every DynamoDB team delivers features faster.

Testing is also central to how DynamoDB speeds up delivery as engineers bring AI agents into their development work. An agent can only correct its own mistakes if it can run a change against a realistic system and see the result. Ready-to-run test clusters give agents that feedback loop. The features this team builds let DynamoDB engineers use AI-assisted development for changes that need more than unit tests, and they let DynamoDB add automated testing to every code review and every release.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate the test infrastructure, frameworks, and tooling that power DynamoDB testing.
- Build test infrastructure that AI agents can use on their own, with clusters ready on demand and results, logs, and metrics an agent can act on.
- Treat DynamoDB engineers as your customers. Reduce how long they wait for test results and how often their tests fail because of infrastructure.
- Own features end to end, from design through deployment and operation, and deliver ambiguous projects with minimal guidance.

Operations and Maintenance:

Amazon Web Services(AWS)のProfessional Servicesでは、企業のオンプレミス環境上にあるワークロードをAWSへのマイグレーションを支援し、これらのシステムをモダナイズすることで、お客様のデジタルトランスフォーメーションをより俊敏かつ弾力的に加速できるようにプロジェクトをリードするCloud Infra Architectを募集しています。

当ポジションのコンサルタントは、お客様とパートナーのオンプレミス環境と稼働するワークロードの評価、計画、動員、設計、実行を支援します。AWS ProServeのコンサルタントは、スケーラブルな移行・モダナイゼーション手法と自動化ツール技術をエンゲージメント全体に適用することで、オンプレミス環境よりクラウドへのマイグレーションおよびモダナイゼーションを加速することを目指します。お客様の経営課題を把握しそれを実現する上で、現行システムのマイグレーションとモダナイゼーションの最適アプローチとそれを実現する全体計画の策定を支援します。また、関係する技術コンサルタントとともに、移行・モダナイゼーションのための最適技術手法や技術選択肢の決定などを支援し、お客様が AWS のサービスを活用してスケーラブルで可用性の高いアプリケーションソリューションを構築できるよう支援します。こうした支援を通じた市場へのサービス投入の短縮化やビジネスインパクトの大きなシステムのクラウドへのマイグレーション＆モダナイゼーションの実現はとてもエキサイティングな経験になるはずです。

descriptionHtml:
Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly workforce and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.


Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Area Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.

Key job responsibilities
- Support, mentor, and motivate your hourly workforce
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Quality Assurance, Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)

title: Quality Assurance Engineer II, Amazon Robotics Systems Quality and Performance Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about quality and robotics? Do you thrive on solving complex problems that span hardware, software, and system integration? Amazon Robotics is looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer II to own quality for robotic systems deployed across Amazon's fulfillment network.

In this role, you won't just execute test plans — you'll define them. You'll take ambiguous product requirements and turn them into comprehensive test strategies covering functional, integration, and performance testing. You'll work hands-on with robotic systems on our test floors, validating that releases meet the quality bar before they reach production sites. When you find problems, you won't just file a bug — you'll trace the root cause across system boundaries and give developers the evidence they need to fix it fast.

You'll also build tools and automation that make the whole team more effective — scripting repeatable test scenarios, developing methods to evaluate release quality, and creating documentation that lets teammates run your tests independently. Your work will multiply the impact of everyone around you. You'll collaborate daily with software engineers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers, representing quality in design reviews, release decisions, and cross-team discussions.

This is a hands-on role based at our BOS27 facility in Westborough, MA. If you want to work at the intersection of robotics, quality engineering, and real-world impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
Own end-to-end test strategy for robotic features and systems — defining what to test, how to test it, and what infrastructure is needed, even when requirements are ambiguous or evolving.
Create and execute test plans for complex test scenarios including system integration, robotic workcell validation, and safety-critical functionality across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries.
Design and build automated test solutions that are maintainable, reusable, and reliable — enabling other engineers to run and extend them independently.
Develop test strategies for non-functional areas such as performance, reliability, and regression detection to ensure product quality is measured objectively.
Isolate, document, and validate defects with detailed evidence and root-cause analysis, enabling development teams to triage and resolve issues efficiently.
Represent quality assurance in cross-functional discussions including design reviews, release readiness decisions, and retrospectives — advocating for quality at every stage of the development lifecycle.
Collaborate with software developers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers to understand technical architecture and assess how changes impact test scope and product behavior.
Mentor junior engineers, interns, and contractors — training them on products, test methodologies, and tools, and creating documentation that reduces tribal knowledge.
Execute testing on physical test floors to qualify releases prior to production deployment, working directly with robotic systems and workcells.
Proactively identify quality risks, propose solutions, and take on projects that improve testing processes or more accurately measure product quality.

A day in the life
Your day starts with a team standup where you and your fellow QA engineers level set on priorities, blockers, and what's happening across active test campaigns. From there, your day might look different depending on where you are in a release cycle.

Some days are heavily hands-on — you're on the test floor at BOS27 running test scenarios against robotic workcells, capturing logs, and investigating unexpected behavior. You'll troubleshoot across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries, pulling data from multiple sources to build a clear picture of what went wrong and why.

Other days are more collaborative — you're in design reviews with software and hardware engineers, asking the questions that shape how a feature gets tested. You might be scoping a test strategy for a new capability, defining what "done" looks like when the requirements are still evolving, or presenting release analysis to stakeholders who need a clear verdict on whether a build is ready for production.

In between, you're building — writing test cases, developing automation that your teammates can pick up and run, creating documentation that eliminates the need for someone to tap you on the shoulder every time. You'll also spend time mentoring junior engineers and contractors, helping them ramp on products and test approaches.

You'll regularly collaborate with software development engineers, systems engineers, hardware engineers, and program managers. Your internal customers are the development teams who depend on your test results to make release decisions, and the operations teams who rely on the quality of what ships to fulfillment sites.

In this role you will work at the intersection of machine learning and physical robotics hardware. You will collaborate with hardware engineers to evaluate how your models perform on real sensors and edge compute, run experiments that directly influence what gets built next, and validate perception systems alongside robotics program teams. You will push the boundaries of computer vision for robotic applications while seeing your work deploy on real robots in real fulfillment centers. This is applied science with immediate, measurable impact at a scale no other robotics company can offer.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. About the team
The Amazon Robotics Quality Assurance Engineering team is a group of approximately 20 engineers supporting a broad portfolio of robotic products and solutions — from manipulation systems and autonomous mobile robots to sortation, storage and retrieval, and outbound dock automation. Our work spans first mile, middle mile, last mile, and outbound dock operations across Amazon's fulfillment network.

We operate across three major test sites in Massachusetts — BOS12 (North Reading), BOS27 (Westborough), and BOS33 (Woburn) — where we maintain dedicated test floors with real robotic workcells and integration environments. We are a mix of hands-on testers, automation builders, and quality strategists who work closely with software, hardware, and systems engineering teams to make sure what ships to production actually works. We are growing and looking for curious, technically strong people who want to make a real impact on how robotics technology serves customers worldwide.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of quality assurance engineering experience
- Experience in automation testing
- Experience in manual testing
- Experience as QA lead on medium to large sized projects

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with at least one automated test framework like Selenium or Appium
- Experience in gathering test requirements to create detailed test plans and defining quality metrics to measure product quality
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
- Experience developing high quality test plans, test designs, test strategies, and test execution
- Experience of using test case management tools (e.g. Test Rail, TestLink) and issue management tools (Jira)
- Experience working closely with development and business teams to communicate problem impacts and to understand business requirements

title: Principal, Senior, Distinguished Engineer, AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services, AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring Principal, Senior, and Distinguished Engineers to join AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services.


AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services is redefining how the world stores, serves, and reasons over data in the age of AI. Our vision is to make every byte of enterprise data instantly durable, infinitely scalable, and intelligent by default — so that organizations of any size can turn their data into insight and action. We pair decades of hard-won operational experience with relentless curiosity to build the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on: object storage (Amazon S3), block storage (Amazon EBS), archival storage (Amazon S3 Glacier), analytics and database engines (Amazon Redshift, EMR, SageMaker), and the ultra-high-performance caching layers that make generative AI and analytics fast and trustworthy at enterprise scale. We're hiring Principal and Senior Principal Engineers across the org to own technical direction for some of our hardest problems: building a new cache product purpose-built for GenAI and analytics — delivering ultra-low-latency, ultra-high-throughput access to S3 data at exponential scale; setting architecture for S3 storage at the exabyte tier; and driving the engineering direction of SageMaker, Redshift, EMR, and AWS Database Services. These are deep, high-ownership systems roles — some remote-eligible, others anchored to hubs like Seattle, Irvine, and Berlin — for engineers who have led org-wide technical strategy and want to see it run in production. If you want to build systems that operate at planet scale — where durability, availability, latency, and failure-mode ownership are first-class concerns measured in eleven nines — this is the team.

What You'll Do

This is a rare chance to own and ship the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on — not features on top of a platform, but the storage, data, and caching layers that everything else depends on, operating at a scale no one else in the industry touches. You'll architect systems that store and serve exabytes of the world's most critical data, where a single design decision ripples across hundreds of millions of customers and millions of applications.

The problems here are unlike anywhere else. How do you deliver eleven nines of durability while adding net-new capabilities to a service that already stores hundreds of trillions of objects? How do you build a new cache product that serves S3 data at ultra-low latency and ultra-high throughput for GenAI and analytics workloads growing exponentially? How do you evolve block, object, and archival storage — and the analytics and database engines on top of them — without ever compromising the durability, availability, and latency guarantees customers have bet their businesses on? These are deep systems challenges solved in production, at a scale where the usual playbooks break down. You help write the new ones.

The systems you build here don't sit in a backlog — they're load-bearing for the internet: S3, EBS, and Glacier storing the data behind modern AI and analytics; Redshift, EMR, and SageMaker turning that data into insight; and the next generation of high-performance caching making all of it fast. You'll have direct influence over technical choices, minimal layers between you and decisions, and the opportunity to define what foundational data infrastructure looks like in the AI era.

Key job responsibilities
Deliver strategic technical projects and design new storage, data, and caching systems at massive scale

Lead architecture and engineering strategy for foundational services across S3, EBS, Glacier, and the analytics and database layer (Redshift, EMR, SageMaker, AWS Database Services)

Mentor and guide engineers while solving the hardest durability, availability, and latency problems hands-on

Work cross-functionally with Principal Engineers and teams across AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services

Scout and recruit top technical talent, actively growing the engineering community

Drive a strong engineering excellence and operational culture across all services and teams

Shape technical direction for systems where correctness, durability, and failure-mode ownership are first-class, measured in eleven nines

Balance deep systems expertise with strong analytical skills to make informed architectural decisions at scale

Basic qualifications

-10+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
-Knowledge of object-oriented design, data structures, and algorithms

Preferred qualifications

-Experience designing and building large-scale systems in a multi-tiered, distributed environment (Service Oriented Architecture)

title: Sr Worldwide Specialist - GenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Data & AI GTM
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to help define the future of Go to Market (GTM) for Amazon Bedrock? In this role, you will define, build, and deploy targeted strategies to accelerate customer adoption of Amazon Bedrock across industry verticals. You will engage with product managers to influence product direction and help customers tap into new markets using Amazon Bedrock alongside other AWS services. Amazon Bedrock hosts a number of foundation models — you will work directly with the model providers on joint GTM plans, joint customer engagements, external/internal evangelism, and demos and proof-of-concepts.

Key job responsibilities
You will define the go-to-market (GTM) strategy for Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore lead cross-functional initiatives to expand existing markets, build scalable adoption programs, and identify new opportunities. Day to day this includes market sizing, partnering with counterparts across the globe to build an opportunity pipeline, working with customers to understand technical requirements, creating content to enable train field teams, driving industry thought leadership, working with product teams to define new features, and identifying partners.

You will drive the GTM plan for scaling adoption of Amazon Bedrock, interact with customers directly to understand their business problems, and work with model providers and solutions architects to define and implement scalable GenAI solutions. You will also work closely with account teams and product teams to unblock and drive production implementations.

The ideal candidate
You bring a business and technology background that lets you lead engagements with customers across segments — from startups to multinational enterprises. You have domain expertise in Generative AI and key ML-powered use cases, and the technical depth to articulate the benefits of Amazon Bedrock and related GenAI services to data scientists and C-level business and technical executives. You understand GenAI market trends, ecosystem, and opportunities, and you are passionate about market development and evangelism. You partner well across AWS (product, solutions architecture, sales, marketing, professional services) and externally with customers and model providers.


A day in the life
You'll partner with AWS service teams, field solutions architecture, sales, and marketing — representing your team to executive management and working directly with AWS's top customers. Inclusive Team Culture

title: Security Engineer II, AWS Cloud Security Response
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Cloud Security Response team operates on the ‘AWS’ side of the Shared Responsibility Model, protecting our customers by ensuring the security of AWS Cloud services. Our engineers independently investigate and resolve security issues across 200+ AWS products, working hands-on with service code, security data, and cloud infrastructure at massive scale.

This role goes beyond coordination. You will apply security judgment to drive outcomes, close security gaps through code, and build automation that scales how we respond to security issues. You will think strategically, identifying patterns that point to systemic risks and driving proactive solutions before issues recur.

We are looking for security professionals who bring deep technical curiosity and the judgment to operate autonomously in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. You will leverage the latest technology and tools to augment your capabilities, and you will partner closely with engineering teams to achieve security outcomes.

Successful candidates should:

- Exercise independent security judgment to assess risk, form informed opinions on severity, and drive engineering teams toward the right outcomes.

- Take a hands-on investigative approach to security issues, building deep technical understanding of risk and customer impact.

- Be technically proficient across security domains including network and operating system security, cryptography, software security, and incident response.

- Communicate complex security issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels.

- Challenge flawed analysis and escalate to senior leadership to ensure the best outcome for customers, even against consensus.

- Work effectively in AI-augmented workflows, using generative AI tools to accelerate security work.

- Mentor and coach junior engineers on security practices and professional growth.

- Drive security outcomes across organizational boundaries, partnering effectively with service teams and peer security teams.

An ideal candidate should be able to conduct most of the following:

- Close security gaps through code, working alongside service teams to develop and validate remediations.

- Navigate complex IAM and access control issues with confidence and technical depth.

- Build automation that improves how the team operates at scale.

- Think proactively, identifying systemic security themes and driving solutions that prevent classes of issues.

- Engage with cloud services at the architectural level, understanding how they work in order to assess and address risk.

Key job responsibilities
- Identify recurring security patterns across AWS services and drive proactive solutions that address root causes and prevent classes of issues.

- Build automation to scale incident response procedures, improving efficiency and reducing manual effort across the team’s global operations.

- Own and drive security issues from identification through resolution, bringing informed risk assessments and security judgment to every engagement with service teams.

- Independently reproduce and validate reported security issues to develop a deep understanding of the vulnerability, its exploitability, and its potential customer impact.

- Investigate and analyze security data across multiple sources to scope the impact of security issues and inform remediation priorities.

- Develop and validate remediations through hands-on code engagement, partnering with service teams to close security issues through code.

- Communicate the state of security issues to technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of seniority, up to and including the AWS Chief Information Security Officer. Escalate when the pace of resolution does not match the impact to customers.

A day in the life
As part of our follow-the-sun rotation, you will receive a handoff from global peers and take ownership of security issues presently in-flight. The issues could relate to any of our 200+ AWS products, so you will often need to learn on-the-fly.

Your first task may be to reproduce a newly reported vulnerability, working through service code and infrastructure to confirm the issue and assess the real-world risk. From there, you will analyze security data to understand whether customers have been impacted and determine the scope. You will engage service team engineers with a clear explanation of the issue, your reproduction details, and your recommended path forward.

As the day progresses, new issues will be assigned to you based on workload. You will triage them, determine their level of impact, and work toward resolution at the appropriate pace. For some issues, you will develop code-level remediations or build automation to address the problem at scale. Throughout the day, you will balance driving individual issues with identifying patterns across your caseload that point to systemic security gaps.

At the end of the day, you will document your work to allow the incoming shift to continue driving issues to resolution.

About the team
Cloud Response is a team within AWS Security Operations. This team is broadly responsible for the ‘AWS’ side of the Shared Responsibility Model, providing oversight of security issues from identification through resolution. Cloud Response operates follow-the-sun with teams based in four geographical locations.

We are evolving toward a model where our engineers are hands-on technical investigators who drive security outcomes through code, automation, and deep understanding of AWS services. We work with AWS service teams to ensure security issues are resolved with the right level of urgency while keeping stakeholders informed throughout the issue lifecycle.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of scripting, programming, and security code review in a common programming language (non-internship) experience
- Bachelor's degree in a STEM field (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), or 2+ years of IT Security experience
- Experience working across teams and influencing teams that are not your own
- Experience in mentoring, leading, or managing more junior engineers
- Experience with cloud services, cloud infrastructure, or cloud security concepts.
- 3+ years of experience in information security, security operations, or security engineering.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience developing code-level fixes or security patches for production cloud services.
- Deep understanding of IAM policies, roles, service principals, and access control mechanisms.
- Experience building automation to scale security operations or incident response processes.
- Experience with proactive security engineering such as identifying systemic patterns, building feedback loops, or driving shift-left security initiatives.
- Experience with AWS services and infrastructure at the code or architecture level.
- 2+ years of working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage experience.

title: Software Development Engineer Intern, Machine Learning/Automated Reasoning- Summer 2027
descriptionHtml:
Shape what comes next | Discover careers in Tech

At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.


What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands.

Our SDE interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As a SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers.

We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth.
________________________

By applying to this position, your application will be considered for Summer 2027 internship roles. All intern roles require in-person work and are 12 weeks in duration, starting in May/June and ending in August/September. Applicants will be considered at all locations we host interns in the United States.

Please note that the majority of our internships are in the Summer of 2027 and applicants will be processed based on business need; however, there may be additional openings that include the following period(s):

1.Fall 2027 (Start August/September; End November/December)

During the application process, you will be given the opportunity to select a preference or interest in other seasonal start dates. Please note that placement in a non-summer season is not guaranteed and is subject to availability.

Amazon internships across all seasons are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work in office, Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day. Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.

We will take your location preferences into consideration. Preferences are based on business availability and are not guaranteed. Applicants will be considered at all locations we host interns in the United States including but not limited to:

• CA (Irvine, San Diego, Sunnyvale)
• TX (Austin)
• MA (Boston)
• NY (New York)
• VA (Arlington)
• WA (Bellevue, Redmond, Seattle)
***Locations are subject to change***

During your application, you will have the opportunity to highlight your expertise in one or more of these specialized areas:

• Machine Learning • Query Processing and Optimization • Automated Reasoning • Prompt Engineering • Distributed Systems

While team placement is based on business needs, sharing your specific skills and interests helps us better align your experience with potential roles.


Key job responsibilities
• Collaborate and communicate effectively with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to design, build, and operate innovative products and services that delight our customers, while participating in technical discussions to drive solutions forward.
• Break down complex, ambiguous problems into well-defined, solvable components before implementation
• Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services, with distributed-systems scope varying by team.
• Participate in code reviews as a core engineering practice, providing constructive feedback and validating correctness, including for AI-generated code.
• Contribute to clear and accurate technical documentation.
• Use GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity, and critically validate, verify, and integrate AI-generated code, exercising sound judgement about when to trust AI output and when not to
• Write clean, maintainable code following best practices and design patterns, including AI-assisted.
• Work in an agile environment practicing CI/CD principles while participating in operational responsibilities including on-call duties.
• Demonstrate operational excellence through monitoring, troubleshooting, and resolving production issues.

A day in the life
As an intern, you will be matched to a manager and a mentor and will have the opportunity to influence the evolution of Amazon technology and lead critical projects early in your career.

In addition to working on an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage with Amazonians for both personal and professional development, expand your network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship. No matter the location of your internship, we give you the tools to own your project and learn in a real-world setting.

Basic qualifications

- Are 18 years of age or older
- Are enrolled in a Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or related STEM fields
- Experience with at least one general-purpose programming language such as Java, Python, C++, C#, Go, Rust, or TypeScript
- Experience with data structure implementation, basic algorithm development, and/or object-oriented design principles
- Experience using AI-assisted development tools in academic or professional settings
- Work 40 hours/week minimum and commit to 12 week internship maximum
- Expected degree conferral date between October 2027 – September 2029
- Have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience from previous technical internship(s) or demonstrated project experience
- Experience with Cloud platforms (preferably AWS), database systems (SQL and NoSQL), AI tools for development productivity, contributing to open-source projects, and/or version control systems
- Knowledge of software development lifecycle, including design, development, test, build, deployment processes and timelines
- Strong problem decomposition, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
- Demonstrated ownership and initiative in seeing work through from design to operation
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Demonstrated ability to learn and adapt to new technologies quickly

title: Data Center Chief Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic Data Center Engineering Operations Team and become a critical architect of the infrastructure that powers global cloud computing. You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of Amazon Web Services' physical infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that support millions of customers worldwide.

The Data Center Chief Engineer (CE) is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response. The CE serves as an expert technical resource interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third-party vendors. They are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations within a given data center and to support AWS.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: PDX is an AWS GovCloud region. As required by our contracts with the federal government, effective February 24, 2026, logical access to the AWS GovCloud region will be restricted to Amazon employees who are U.S. Citizens. (GovCloud may NOT be accessed from outside of the United States).

NOTE: Relocation assistance will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
Act as the primary escalation point for all facilities-related issues. Oversee operation and management of routine and emergency services on a variety of critical systems such as switchgear, generators, UPS systems, power distribution equipment, chillers, cooling towers, computer room air handlers, building monitoring systems, etc.

Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures and troubleshooting of facility within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA).

Provide training and guidance to Engineering Operations Technicians and are responsible for working with Facility Manager (FM) to set team culture.

Create and deploy new standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams

May assist in the building out of new facilities and assist in projects to increase current facility efficiency

Working outside of normal business hours for routine maintenance as required, including responding to out-of-hours emergency calls.

Communicate complex technical information to a non-technical audience.

Work with IT managers and other business leaders to coordinate projects, manage capacity, and optimize plant safety, performance, reliability and efficiency

Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff

Establish building performance benchmarks, conduct analyses, and prepare reports on all aspects of the critical facility of operations and maintenance.

Utilize Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook and other basic administrative tools to perform day-to-day tasks



Physical Requirements:

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodation:

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection



Essential Requirements:

Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including electrical support equipment that supports servers that must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. Equipment will include but is not limited to stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

The CE directs, trains and supports technicians in their role of providing hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. Implementation and execution of site/equipment-specific training exercises is also expected. They manage projects from conception to completion. These projects involve independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, processing, and finance in both local and global settings. The CE will be tasked with creating and delivering on key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities.


About the team

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager- Software , Annapurna Labs
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs builds the custom silicon and software behind AWS, including the AWS Nitro System, Graviton, and the Inferentia/Trainium machine learning accelerators. That software runs on millions of AWS servers and supports every EC2 customer.

The role
We're looking for a Senior TPM to drive large, cross-team software programs from planning through production. You'll work with engineering teams in Israel and the US, and with AWS service teams. You'll turn ambiguous goals into clear plans, own software release and deployment programs, and raise how well the org delivers. This is a technical role: you'll go deep on architecture, dependencies and tradeoffs with engineers and senior leaders.


Key job responsibilities
Own multi-team software programs end to end: new feature development, major releases, and fleet-wide deployments.
Define scope, milestones, dependencies and success metrics with engineering managers and principal engineers.
Run the program cadence: roadmaps, schedules, risk tracking, status reviews and launch readiness.
Own the software release process: release planning, quality gates, branching and versioning, and go/no-go decisions.
Drive safe deployment to the AWS fleet with service teams: rollout plans, monitoring and rollback readiness.
Find risks early, lead tradeoff decisions on scope, schedule and quality, and escalate clearly.
Improve how engineering works through better processes, tools and metrics (CI/CD, test coverage, delivery speed, operational excellence).
Write clear narratives (PR/FAQs, 6-pagers, program and operational reviews) for leadership up to VP level.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a sync between the driver and firmware teams, where you sort out a dependency that's putting the next release at risk. You'll update the plan and agree on next steps before lunch.

Midday, you might join an architecture review with principal engineers on a new feature. You'll ask questions about scope, test strategy and rollout risk, and turn the discussion into milestones the teams can commit to.

In the afternoon, you could be leading a go/no-go meeting for a software release. You'll review quality gates, test results and open issues, then coordinate a safe, gradual rollout across the AWS fleet with partner service teams.

You'll finish the day writing a short program update for leadership: what's on track, what's at risk, and the decisions you need from them. Some days you'll write a PR/FAQ or 6-pager for a new initiative. On others you'll work with US-based teams in the evening to keep global work moving.

No two weeks look the same. One week you're supporting bring-up of new hardware, the next you're improving the CI/CD pipeline or running an operational review after an incident. The common thread is that you own outcomes, not just schedules.

About the team
Annapurna Labs is the AWS team that designs the custom chips behind the AWS cloud, including the AWS Nitro System, Graviton processors, and the Inferentia and Trainium machine learning accelerators. Our engineers in Israel work across the full stack, from chip design to the software that runs on millions of servers in AWS data centers.

Our software organization based in Haifa and Tel Aviv builds the low-level software that brings Annapurna's hardware to life: device drivers, firmware and hardware abstraction layers. This software sits between the chip and the AWS services above it. It has to be fast, secure and reliable at very large scale, because every EC2 customer depends on it.

As a TPM in this org, you'll sit at the center of the software lifecycle. You'll work with driver, firmware and platform teams, plus partner teams across AWS, to plan, build, release and deploy software from first bring-up to production. You'll be joining a small, senior team that operates like a startup inside AWS, with high ownership and direct impact on AWS infrastructure.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Transportation Specialist
descriptionHtml:
TOC (Transportation Operation Center) is the central command and control center for ‘Transportation Execution’ across the Amazon Supply Chain network supporting multiple geographies like NA, India and EU. It ensures hassle free, timely pick-up and delivery of freight from vendors to Amazon fulfillment centers (FC) and from Amazon FCs to carrier hubs. In case of any exceptions, TOC steps in to resolve the issue and keeps all the stakeholders informed on the proceedings. Along with this tactical problem solving TOC is also charged with understanding trends in network exceptions and then automating processes or proposing process changes to streamline operations. This second aspect involves network monitoring and significant analysis of network data.
Overall, TOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time.
Purview of a Trans Ops Specialist
A Trans Ops Specialist at TOC facilitates flow of information between different stakeholders (Trans Carriers/Hubs/Warehouses) and resolves any potential issues that impacts customer experience and business continuity. Trans Ops Specialist at TOC works across two verticals – Inbound and Outbound operations.
Inbound Operations deals with Vendor/Carrier/FC relationship, ensuring that the freight is picked-up on time and is delivered at FC as per the given appointment. Trans Ops Specialist on Inbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of pick-up to delivery.
Outbound Operations deals with FC/Carrier/Carrier Hub relationship, ensuring that the truck leaves the FC in order to delivery customer orders as per promise. Trans Ops Specialist on Outbound addresses any potential issues occurring during the lifecycle of freight leaving the FC and reaching customer premises.

A Trans Ops Specialist provides timely resolution to the issue in hand by researching and querying internal tools and by taking real-time decisions. An ideal candidate should be able to understand the requirements/be able to analyze data and notice trends and be able to drive Customer Experience without compromising on time. The candidate should have the basic understanding of Logistics and should be able to communicate clearly in the written and oral form. Trans Ops Specialist should be able to ideate process improvements and should have the zeal to drive them to conclusion.


Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

· Communication with external customers (Carriers, Vendors/Suppliers) and internal customers (Retail, Finance, Software Support, Fulfillment Centers)
· Ability to pull data from numerous databases (using Excel, Access, SQL and/or other data management systems) and to perform ad hoc reporting and analysis as needed is a plus.
· Develop and/or understand performance metrics to assist with driving business results.
· Ability to scope out business and functional requirements for the Amazon technology teams who create and enhance the software systems and tools are used by TOC.
· Must be able to quickly understand the business impact of the trends and make decisions that make sense based on available data.
· Must be able to systematically escalate problems or variance in the information and data to the relevant owners and teams and follow through on the resolutions to ensure they are delivered.
· Work within various time constraints to meet critical business needs, while measuring and identifying activities performed.
· Excellent communication, both verbal and written as one may be required to create a narrative outlining weekly findings and the variances to goals, and present these finding in a review forum.
